proceduralStep.title: Software Loading Overview
proceduralStep.para: Indicating and Recording System software resides in multiple locations:

- Display Management Computers (DMC): Display rendering and formatting applications
- Crew Alerting Computers (CAC): Alert logic and prioritization
- IMA Modules: Hosted applications for data processing and routing
- Data Acquisition Units (DAU): Firmware for signal conditioning and encoding
- Recorders (FDR/CVR/QAR): Embedded recorder firmware
Software loading procedures vary by LRU type. This data module provides general methodology.

proceduralStep.title: Pre-Loading Verification
proceduralStep.para: WARNING: Loading incorrect software can cause system failure or loss of critical functions.
Verify software part number matches aircraft configuration. Check Software Configuration Management (SCM) database for compatibility matrix.
Verify digital signature of software package using OEM-provided public key certificate. Loading tool will validate signature automatically.
Record current software version from each target LRU for rollback capability.
Ensure aircraft on ground, parking brake set, and non-essential electrical loads OFF.
Connect maintenance laptop to aircraft Ethernet port (typically in avionics bay or cockpit).
Launch software loading tool on maintenance laptop.
Select target LRU: Display Management Computer (identify by serial number/position).
Verify network connectivity to target LRU. Tool will display CONNECTED or OFFLINE status.
Select software load file (.lod or .zip format) from USB or downloaded location.
Initiate software transfer. Progress bar shows upload percentage. DO NOT interrupt power during this phase.
After transfer complete, LRU will automatically verify checksum and initiate installation.
LRU will reboot automatically (takes 30-60 seconds). Monitor for successful restart.
Tool displays LOAD SUCCESSFUL or LOAD FAILED status.
If load failed, LRU automatically reverts to previous software version. Review error log and retry.
Repeat process for redundant DMC (DMC-2) to maintain software version consistency.

proceduralStep.title: Configuration Data Loading
proceduralStep.para: Configuration data defines system parameters, alert thresholds, display formats, and operational modes. Configuration loading follows similar process to software loading but typically faster.
Select target LRU and choose LOAD CONFIGURATION option in loading tool.
Select configuration file (.cfg or .xml format) specific to aircraft tail number and configuration.
Tool transfers and verifies configuration data.
LRU validates configuration against software version compatibility matrix.
If validation passes, configuration activated immediately (no reboot required unless specified).
Verify configuration loaded correctly by reviewing system setup pages on maintenance display.
Power-cycle entire indicating and recording system (de-energize and re-energize master CBs).
Verify all LRUs complete power-up self-test with no faults.
Access software version page on maintenance display and confirm new software versions displayed.
Perform functional test per DMC-AMPEL360-31-00-00-520B (calibration and functional checks).
Execute BITE test suite per DMC-AMPEL360-31-00-00-520A. All tests should PASS.
Perform operational check: Cycle through display pages, inject test alerts, verify recording system status.
If any test fails, investigate fault and repeat software loading if necessary.

proceduralStep.title: Data Integrity Verification
proceduralStep.para: After software/configuration loading, verify data integrity of critical parameters:
Access data integrity check menu: MFD → MAINTENANCE → DATA INTEGRITY.
System performs automatic checksums on:

- Executable code (CRC-32 or SHA-256)
- Configuration databases
- Alert logic tables
- Display format definitions
- Calibration coefficients
Compare checksums against expected values documented in software release notes.
If any checksum mismatch detected, reload affected data and re-verify.
System continuously monitors data integrity during operation. Any corruption detected generates BITE fault code.
Update aircraft configuration control records with new software versions and load dates.
Record software part numbers, revision levels, and checksums in aircraft maintenance log.
Update Digital Product Passport (DPP) with software baseline change.
If software change affects operational limitations or procedures, notify flight operations and update Flight Manual Supplements if required.
Archive previous software versions and configuration files for rollback capability (minimum 2 previous versions retained).

proceduralStep.title: Software Rollback Procedure
proceduralStep.para: If new software causes operational issues, rollback to previous version:
Locate archived previous software version and configuration files.
Follow standard software loading procedure using previous version files.
After rollback, perform complete functional and BITE testing.
Document rollback reason and notify OEM of software issue for investigation.

proceduralStep.title: Cybersecurity Considerations
proceduralStep.para: WARNING: Software loading process includes multiple cybersecurity controls. Do not attempt to bypass:

- Digital signature verification (prevents unauthorized or malicious software)
- Secure boot (ensures only authenticated software executes)
- Version compatibility checks (prevents incompatible software combinations)
- Audit logging (all software changes logged with timestamp and user ID)
- Access control (only authorized personnel can load software)
Any cybersecurity control violation will generate BITE fault and prevent software installation.
